news.title: Anthropic’s Big Reveal
news.summary: The tech industry equivalent of the Super Bowl may finally be upon us. Anthropic could make public the paperwork for its initial public offering as early as Monday. Details about Anthropic’s finances from either drafts of the IPO filing or recent investor meetings have been dribbling out for weeks. As a result, some of the S-1’s revelations will not be, well, all that revelatory. But there are still many, many mysteries about Anthropic the filing could clear up, or at least make a little less fuzzy. I asked my colleagues Jason Dean and Laura Mandaro for their shortlist of items they hope the S-1 will illuminate: • More financial details. More clarity on Anthropic’s trajectory toward profitability, along with cash flow numbers and other operational financial metrics that haven’t yet leaked out. • Ownership, investment and revenue details from big partners. Hopefully, the filing will confirm just how much money Anthropic is paying Google and Amazon to run its AI on their servers, along with details about how much those companies invested in Anthropic and how much those stakes have appreciated. • Who pays Anthropic’s bills. Anthropic has said around a fifth of its revenue this quarter

news.title: Can the AI Boom Survive a Margin Squeeze?
news.summary: In this episode of Merryn Talks Money, Merryn Somerset Webb and Steve Hou, head of research at Silicon Data, delve into an emerging issue in the economics of artificial intelligence: token prices are falling while the cost of compute needed to produce them is rising. (Source: Bloomberg)

news.title: Stripe’s AI Shopping Lead Puts Card Giants on Edge
news.summary: As AI assistants like Instinct and Meta Platforms’ Muse start to gain traction in shopping, Stripe has taken a leading position in how the agents pay. That’s putting the credit card giants on edge. The reason for their apprehension: Stripe in many cases is enabling AI agent purchases through virtual cards for one-time use, which can leave card networks with less control over the shopping and payment process, people who work closely with the card firms say. Mastercard and Visa have developed their own payment technology for agent shopping that would use customers’ existing cards, giving the card companies more visibility into who’s making what purchases. That method is still at an early stage, though.

items.title: Stripe’s AI Shopping Lead Puts Card Giants on Edge
items.summary: As AI assistants like Instinct and Meta Platforms’ Muse start to gain traction in shopping, Stripe has taken a leading position in how the agents pay. That’s putting the credit card giants on edge. The reason for their apprehension: Stripe in many cases is enabling AI agent purchases through virtual cards for one-time use, which can leave card networks with less control over the shopping and payment process, people who work closely with the card firms say. Mastercard and Visa have developed their own payment technology for agent shopping that would use customers’ existing cards, giving the card companies more visibility into who’s making what purchases. That method is still at an early stage, though.
